clue.text: What the lady did in a railway carriage is hidden at first

parts.note: a van is a railway carriage for luggage or goods
taken as written

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the word hidden

explanation.surface: A clue recalling the Hitchcock film where an old lady disappears from a train compartment.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lady Vanishes is Hitchcock's film about a woman who disappears on a train; 'at first' takes the H of 'hidden'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the film's title the lady disappears, so what she did was disappear from sight.

clue.text: Lady Nicolson at length seen in an old theatre to publicize Rising

parts.note: the Old Vic is a London theatre, so VIC stands for it
taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means this word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to air an opinion is to publicize it

explanation.surface: Vita Sackville-West's full name appearing on a playbill at a famous old playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Vita Sackville-West, wife of Harold Nicolson, was christened with this longer name; 'Rising' turns AIR into RIA. The Old Vic is a London theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Vita Sackville-West, Lady Nicolson, used a short form of her full baptismal name, so 'at length' asks for the unabridged version.

clue.text: Ulster author turns up in equipment for game

parts.note: NI, Northern Ireland, is often called Ulster

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means this word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a pen is a writer, as in a hired pen
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Northern Irish writer making an appearance amid sports kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'author' here means a writer in the loose sense of a hired pen; Ulster is the common name for Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Each skittle in the bowling game of skittles is a piece of the game's kit.

clue.text: Desirable topic for 17

parts.note: the play by the dramatist at 17 is A ___ Named Desire, so its subject is the vehicle bearing that name

explanation.walkthrough: 17 is Tennessee Williams, whose most famous play's vehicle is 'named Desire'.
explanation.definitionFit: The tram in Williams's play bears the name Desire, so it is the desirable subject of his work.

clue.text: "Or quick — darting through the brain" (Pope, Essay on Man)

definitions.text: "Or quick — darting through the brain" (Pope, Essay on Man)

parts.words: "Or quick — darting through the brain" (Pope, Essay on Man)
parts.note: the missing word completes Pope's line from Epistle I of An Essay on Man

explanation.walkthrough: A quotation clue: Pope's line reads 'Or quick effluvia darting through the brain', from Epistle I of An Essay on Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Pope imagines invisible emanations or vapours flashing through the mind, so the gap takes his word for such outflows.

clue.text: They have no vehicle with which to pay on Robert Silverberg's account

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another sits above it

parts.note: to foot a bill is to pay it
Passengers is a Nebula-winning short story by Robert Silverberg

explanation.surface: Walkers who must pay their way, as described in a science-fiction story.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Silverberg is an American science-fiction writer; 'account' here means story.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrians travel on foot rather than in any car or carriage.

clue.text: Like Banquo to Macbeth, murdered ally with nothing to gain

indicators.note: to gain says the scrambled word takes in the letter for nothing
murdered suggests the word ally is mangled into a new order

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Macbeth's friend Banquo, faithful yet murdered with nothing to show for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'murdered' rearranges ALLY to LYAL, and 'to gain' puts O inside after the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Banquo was faithful to Macbeth, a steadfast friend and fellow general, before Macbeth had him killed.

clue.text: Sarah — singer and scandalous novelist

definitions.meaning: Sarah ... was an American jazz singer
Sarah ... is also a British novelist, author of Anatomy of a Scandal

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sarah' serves both senses: two different women share the full name.
explanation.definitionFit: The jazz vocalist and the author of a political courtroom thriller share the same full name.

clue.text: Detests executioner on leaving

indicators.note: leaving signals that the little word on departs from the name

parts.note: Abhorson is the executioner in Shakespeare's Measure for Measure
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone loathes the hangman as he walks away.
explanation.walkthrough: Abhorson is the executioner in Shakespeare's Measure for Measure; 'leaving' removes ON from his name.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe something intensely is to hate it, the plain synonym here.

clue.text: Right off girl's eager as men in play (by 17)

indicators.note: in play suggests the gathered letters are set moving into a new order
off says the letter for right is removed from the word before it

parts.note: the possessive read as plain letters
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl and some men eagerly caught up in a theatrical production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes R from GIRLS, leaving GILS; 'in play' then rearranges GILS, EAGER, AS and MEN. 17 is Tennessee Williams.
explanation.definitionFit: The Glass Menagerie is a memory play written by Tennessee Williams, the dramatist at 17.

clue.text: E.g. Kathleen Ferrier in control at broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A celebrated English singer at the radio microphone, running the show.
explanation.walkthrough: Kathleen Ferrier was a celebrated English singer of the 1940s and 50s, much heard on BBC radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferrier sang in the lowest female vocal range, so she is an example of that voice type.

clue.text: A lad described by Tolstoy and Conrad

definitions.meaning: both Tolstoy and Joseph Conrad wrote works with this one-word title

explanation.definitionFit: A boy in his teens is a young person, and the word also names works by both writers.

clue.text: He pours out his heart musically

definitions.text: He pours out his heart musically

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the words beside it are put into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A singer emotionally baring his soul in song.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: 'out' rearranges HE POURS, and the legendary musician famously poured out his grief in song.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical Thracian musician sang his grief for Eurydice so movingly that he charmed the underworld.

clue.text: Might a thief, quietly replacing a bit of furniture, be seen in her empty house?

indicators.note: replacing says one letter takes the place of another in the word for a thief

parts.note: a filcher is someone who pilfers small things

indicators.note: a bit of asks for just the first letter of furniture

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A burglar creeping round a vacant house, swapping furniture about.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosamunde Pilcher wrote the novel The Empty House, so 'her empty house' points to its author. P replaces F, the first letter of 'furniture'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosamunde Pilcher's 1973 novel is titled The Empty House, so the house belongs to her as its writer.

clue.text: Greek musical mode, one that's mostly pleasant about start of oratorio

indicators.note: about means the first pieces go round the next one

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral, is one

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: nice means pleasant

indicators.note: start of asks for the opening letter of oratorio

explanation.surface: A Greek mode described as mostly agreeable around the opening of a choral work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims NICE to NIC; I plus NIC goes 'about' O, the start of 'oratorio'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Greek music named its modes after peoples and regions, one being from Ionia.

clue.text: Amelia Havisham's status, cooped up, wasted

parts.note: Dickens's Havisham in Great Expectations is an unmarried woman, so her title is Miss
pent means shut in, as in pent-up

explanation.surface: Dickens's jilted spinster, shut away in her house, a life thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: Miss Havisham is the jilted bride in Dickens's Great Expectations who never leaves her house.
explanation.definitionFit: A misspent life is one wasted or squandered, as Miss Havisham's arguably was.

clue.text: Soldier's locations revealed in S Korean movie

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier; the 's links to the next word
sites are locations

explanation.surface: Military positions disclosed in a South Korean film.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Soldier's' gives no letter. Parasite is Bong Joon-ho's Oscar-winning South Korean film.
explanation.definitionFit: Bong Joon-ho's 2019 film won the Academy Award for Best Picture, the first non-English-language winner.

clue.text: Novelists Charles, John, and Nigel want Amis displaced

parts.note: to will something is to want it

indicators.note: displaced means the letters of Amis are moved out of place

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Several novelists envying the novelist Amis and wishing him gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displaced' rearranges AMIS to IAMS. Charles, John and Nigel share a surname with Tennessee, the playwright behind clues 3, 9 and 22.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles, John and Nigel are all writers of fiction sharing one common Welsh surname.

clue.text: He described a lovely lady, a sailor dressed in fine fabric

indicators.note: dressed in means the sailor is clothed by the fabric, sitting inside it

parts.note: lace is a delicate fabric
a Wren is a member of the Women's Royal Naval Service

explanation.surface: A woman in the navy wearing delicate lace, admired by a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: D. H. Lawrence wrote the short story The Lovely Lady. A Wren is a woman sailor in the British navy.
explanation.definitionFit: D. H. Lawrence wrote a 1927 short story titled The Lovely Lady, so he is its author.

clue.text: Lofty, head lowered, getting on, in summary

indicators.note: in a down clue the head of the word drops to its foot

parts.note: lofty means tall
getting on means growing old

explanation.surface: A tall person growing older, put briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head lowered' moves the T of TALL to the end, giving ALLT.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means taken as a whole, in total, a way of summing up.

clue.text: One introducing books into Bible classes?

definitions.text: One introducing books into Bible classes?

indicators.note: into means these pieces go inside the letters for Bible classes

parts.note: RI, religious instruction, is a school subject teaching the Bible
A means one, here the one leading in front of the books
B is the abbreviation for book, so BB is books

explanation.surface: A teacher bringing books of scripture into religious lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: RI is religious instruction in British schools. The whole clue also describes a Jewish teacher of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher, someone who introduces pupils to the books of scripture.

clue.text: Nero's Swiss chef, who might have burnt the food?

definitions.meaning: Fritz ... is the Swiss cook to Rex Stout's detective Nero Wolfe

definitions.text: who might have burnt the food?
definitions.meaning: in German the word means a burner, so a joke about scorched cooking

explanation.walkthrough: Nero is Rex Stout's detective Nero Wolfe, not the emperor; his chef Fritz shares his surname with the German for 'burner'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fritz Brenner cooks for Nero Wolfe in Rex Stout's detective novels, and his surname means burner in German.

clue.text: Nocturnal creature according to 17

parts.note: Tennessee Williams, at 17, wrote The Night of the ___, so the animal in that title is of the night

explanation.walkthrough: 17 is Tennessee Williams; his play The Night of the Iguana puts the lizard in the night.
explanation.definitionFit: The lizard of Williams's play title belongs to the night, which makes it nocturnal by his account.

clue.text: A tale of secret code, or a virus?

definitions.meaning: Edgar Allan Poe's story about a cipher leading to buried treasure
a computer virus of the 1990s bore this name

explanation.definitionFit: Poe's story turns on cracking a cryptogram, and a 1990s computer virus took the same name.

clue.text: A 20 mostly mauled by an elephant

indicators.note: mauled means the letters are mangled into a new order
mostly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: the answer to 20 across, a Jewish teacher

explanation.surface: A Jewish teacher savaged by an elephant.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is RABBI; 'mostly' trims it to RABB, and 'mauled' rearranges A plus RABB.
explanation.definitionFit: Babar is the elephant king of Jean de Brunhoff's French picture books.

clue.text: Are her novels full of garrulous talk and grace mostly?

definitions.text: Are her novels full of garrulous talk and grace mostly?

parts.note: gas is idle chatter

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: Grace Kelly, the film star, gives the surname

explanation.surface: A question about whether a Victorian novelist's books are all chatter and graciousness.
explanation.walkthrough: Grace Kelly was the American actress who became Princess of Monaco; 'mostly' cuts KELLY to KELL. Elizabeth Gaskell's Cranford is famous for gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth Gaskell's novels such as Cranford are known for gossipy talk and gentle grace.

clue.text: A theatrical failure that was devastating

parts.note: in American theatre slang a show that bombs is a flop

explanation.surface: A stage flop that was a disaster for everyone involved.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition phrase stands for the noun: an atomic weapon is a thing that was devastating.
explanation.definitionFit: The atomic weapon dropped in 1945 caused catastrophic destruction.

clue.text: Imaginary kingdom in which 3 Queen has no time to follow Capek play

indicators.note: to follow puts the shortened queen after the play's initials

parts.note: R.U.R. is Karel Capek's robot play

indicators.note: has no means a letter is taken away

parts.note: Titania is queen of the fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: A fairy queen in a made-up realm, tagging along after a Czech play.
explanation.walkthrough: The '3' does not fit any reading as a cross-reference; the queen is Titania from A Midsummer Night's Dream, losing a T. Ruritania is Anthony Hope's kingdom in The Prisoner of Zenda.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Hope invented this Central European realm for The Prisoner of Zenda.

clue.text: Author with Irish name? Hardly

parts.note: and means with, joining things
Erse is the Irish Gaelic language

explanation.surface: Is a writer with a Gaelic-sounding name Irish? Not likely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardly' teases: the writer of fairy tales was Danish, not Irish at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Hans Christian Andersen was the Danish writer of fairy tales such as The Little Mermaid.

clue.text: Old Master is one to worship

parts.note: sir is a form of address for a master
taken as written

explanation.surface: A great old painting worthy of reverence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Master' looks like a painter; it splits into O and SIR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian god of the dead was venerated across ancient Egypt.
